name: Range
author: Shadow Software

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: TOME4_AMOSPro.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: Ships with TOME IV and is a superset of the build on the PD CD — 73 keywords against 48, and the smaller table is a strict PREFIX of this one, so ONE port serves both. Version off the binary: the title string at $167a is `AMOS Pro Club Extension V2.9Plus`. Slot 9 off the binary, twice: `move.l a3,$178(a5)` and `moveq #$8,d0`. This build is AMOS Pro ONLY and checks — routine 0 opens `cmp.l #$41506578,d1` ('APex') and returns $ff otherwise, which is why the two files are named Range.Lib and AMOSPro_Range.Lib. Routine 0's $361f0f / $369e99 are PAULA_CLOCK_PAL and PAULA_CLOCK_NTSC, the divisor Sam Speed uses. DEFECT: the TOKEN TABLE is malformed. `splot`'s entry (id 1134) has no `-1` after its `I0,0,0,0` spec, and `Ver_Ech` (+Verif.s:5259) ends a field at the first NEGATIVE byte — so the walk runs on through the assembler's $00 pad, through the next entry's `dc.w $004d,$ffff`, through its name `float planes`, and stops at THAT entry's terminator. The result is one 22-byte entry where there should be two: `splot` keeps its name and routine but carries the spec `I0,0,0,0\0\0M`, and the table re-syncs one entry late on the fragment `t planes` (id 1156) whose routine numbers are the ASCII `fl`/`oa` of the swallowed name. So routine 77 is unreachable and `T Planes` jumps to routine 26220. AMOS reads it the same way on a real Amiga, so the table is kept verbatim rather than repaired. It is the only one of the 91 libraries held with a control character in a spec. This was previously recorded here as extdis miscalibrating the jump table ("28,514 routines") because extdis derived that count from the highest routine number a TOKEN named — i.e. from the fragment. It now comes from the jump table, which reports 94, and extdis flags the stray entry.
